title: Scotland Forever? Not With This Drugs Policy!

content_html_sanitized:
Scotland has always “punched above its weight”. With only about five million people, less than 10 percent of the population of the UK, it has played a major role in history. Unfortunately, today it may be the saddest part of the decline of a not so great Great Britain.

 

I should note that Cowan is a Scottish name, and almost all of my ancestors came from England, Scotland and Wales, so there is not the slightest schadenfreude in my saying that. I loved visiting Edinburgh, a truly beautiful city, but my memories are saddened by what has and has not happened in the meantime.

 

What has happened?

From last August, see Scotland’s drug deaths remain worst in Europe amid ‘concerning’ 12% increase. Government pledges to step up efforts to tackle the problem as figures show the number of deaths rose to 1,172 in 2023.

 

Tragectly, “The number of deaths involving bromazolam – a type of benzodiazepine used to treat anxiety disorders, insomnia and seizures – rose from 54 in 2022 to 426 last year.”

 

It is important to note that this tragedy did not happen as the result of some permissive policy. On the contrary, Britain has some of the most restrictive drug laws in Western Europe.

 

“Cannabis is a Class B drug in Scotland. Cannabis is illegal to possess, produce or distribute. Prison sentences of 5 to 14 years and unlimited fines are possible under current laws.”

 

Nonetheless, “Fifteen-year-old boys in Scotland have the highest rate for smoking cannabis according to a new report from the World Health Organization (WHO). The study found that nearly a quarter (23%) of boys aged 15 in Scotland surveyed said they had tried the Class B drug at some point.”

 

Unfortunately, Scottish drug laws are controlled by the Parliament in London, not in Edinburgh. Until recently it seemed unlikely that Edinburgh would demand some sort of reform, and the Parliament in London seems to live in fear of the Prohibitionists tabloids.

 

Medical cannabis is finally available in the UK if you can convince a doctor that you have suffered long enough without it.

See Cannabis-based products for medicinal use (CBPMs)

“This is a summary of key information on medicinal cannabis to support prescribers. It outlines information to support, prescribing and outlines the legal position for CBPMs.”

Medical cannabis social clubs are being organized, but have faced a lot of challenges, including opposition from the local police.See The Rise and Fall of UK Cannabis Social Clubs

So we can be cautiously optimistic. I have a lot of experience with that, but read this from 2002.

What has not happened:Founder of Edinburghs First Coffee Shop Issues Challenge to the UK Government: Give us twelve months to show that there is a solution... A Brilliantly Practical Suggestion.

How time flies, when you’re not in pain or you’re not in prison.
